objective: TWIST-3D-20261025-001 closed the bit level: with one bit per edge, counting laws on ordered triangulations see a closed three-manifold only through |H1(M; Z2)|. Ask what larger distinctions, patterns of bits, let counting see: classify the counting laws whose triangle rule makes the long edge a function of the two short edges, on any finite set of labels with the function total or partial, under the ordered 2-3 and 1-4 moves; census every triangle relation on three labels and every multiplication table on four. Hypothesis under test: only groups survive, so the counts are homomorphism counts of the fundamental group. Nearest known work: the Dijkgraaf-Witten and Wakui state sums for finite groups on ordered triangulations, their groupoid versions, and the Duskin-Glenn characterization of groupoid nerves by unique horn fillers. Standalone value: how much composite structure a counting law needs to see which three-dimensional topology, and what no count can see.
status: Complete 2026-10-25: patterns of patterns in three dimensions. The ordered moves force a groupoid: a counting law whose long edge is a function of the two short edges survives exactly when its working triangles are the compositions of a finite groupoid with equal component values, so its count is a sum of |Hom(pi1(M), G)|/|G| and sees a three-manifold only through the finite quotients of its fundamental group (lens spaces of equal order look alike). All 2^27 relations on three labels and all 4^16 tables on four labels confirm it: only groupoid laws, with free decorations, survive. Next: where counting in three dimensions becomes hard (2/3); execution deferred to the owner.
title: Patterns of patterns in three dimensions
